interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is driven by several concerning factors, including a preoperative PSA of 190 and positive surgical margins with seminal vesicle invasion. The pathological findings indicate an advanced local disease burden, evidenced by the presence of lymphovascular invasion and documented lymph node metastasis. A countervailing finding is the ISUP grade group 2 diagnosis from the prostatectomy specimen, which is lower than the Gleason 4+3 seen on biopsy. Furthermore, the nodal status was sampled, providing a definitive assessment rather than widening uncertainty due to missing sampling. The postoperative PSA trajectory remains unknown, and this information would significantly revise the prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 34.46 months. This is a predicted recurrence horizon, not evidence of observed recurrence. The sensitivity range is 25.85–43.08 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text:
The prognosis is driven by several concerning factors, including a preoperative PSA of 190 and positive surgical margins. Pathological findings reveal extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, lymphovascular invasion, and documented lymph node metastasis. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy comparison shows an upgrade in Gleason grade from the biopsy (4+3/ISUP 3) to the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 3+4/ISUP 2), though both indicate significant cancer.

Countervailing findings are limited, as no negative factors were explicitly documented regarding nodal status beyond the presence of metastasis. Missing postoperative PSA and follow-up data significantly widen uncertainty regarding future risk stratification. Future prognosis revision would depend critically on obtaining a postoperative PSA value and tracking its subsequent trajectory over time.
